item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Thu Oct 15, 8:00 AM — Marin Veterans' Memorial Auditorium
item.description:
Price: Free
Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market.
Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine.
www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Dem

item.title: Pulp Painting — Sat Oct 17, 10:00 AM — North Bay Letterpress Arts
item.description:
Using finely-beaten, pigmented paper pulp, students will make imagery on freshly pulled sheets of handmade paper. Participants will learn introductory handmade paper techniques such as Western sheet formation, as well as surface design methods of pulp painting, stenciling, and inclusions. When dried, pulp paintings are a part of the paper itself! Elements such as photos, hair, leaves, and newspaper clippings can be embedded into newly made sheets of paper or by using methyl cellulose as an adhesive. Please be aware that papermaking is a wet activity – wear clothing and shoes that can get wet. Class involves some physical activity, including standing and arm movements. All supplies are provided through the materials fee. La maestra habla español.
Source: Sebastopol Calendar

item.title: Harvest Table at Somerston Estate – October — Sat Oct 17, 12:00 PM — Somerston Estate
item.description:
Harvest is drawing to a close, and there’s no better time to experience the culmination of the season at Somerston Estate. Join us for an unforgettable afternoon featuring a seasonal lunch expertly paired with estate wines, all set against the stunning backdrop of our vineyards as another remarkable vintage nears completion.
Executive Winemaker Cody Hurd will join us to reflect on the season’s triumphs and challenges, sharing insights from the harvest along with a special harvest-inspired experience exclusive to the day. From the final fruit coming in to stories from the cellar, this is a rare opportunity to connect with the people and passion behind every bottle.
Raise a glass to another extraordinary harvest while enjoying exceptional food, world-class wines, and the unparalleled beauty of Somerston Estate.
Source: Press Democrat

item.title: Reuse in Art, Reuse in Life: A Conversation Between Ali Gass and Phoebe Schenker — Sun Oct 18, 3:30 PM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join Alison Gass, Founding Executive Director of the ICA San Francisco, and Phoebe Schenker, Executive Director of Reuse Alliance, for a wide-ranging conversation about reuse in contemporary and historical art and why it is more relevant than ever.
The discussion will explore the many ways artists have engaged with reuse, from incorporating found and reclaimed materials to making reuse itself a central subject of their work. Together, Gass and Schenker will consider how reuse connects to broader cultural conversations about creativity, sustainability, consumption, and value, while also exploring how reuse can become a creative practice in our own everyday lives.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Hosting 101 at Great Company — Thu Oct 22, 6:00 PM — Great Company
item.description:
You’ve said “we should get together” a hundred times. This is the class where you actually do it.
Hosting isn’t about a perfect house, matching napkins, or a fancy menu. It’s about opening the door and making people feel glad they came. Over one relaxed evening around our table, we’ll walk through the whole arc of having people over: who to invite and how to ask, how to set up so you’re not stuck in the kitchen, and what to do in those first awkward ten minutes when everyone arrives.
Then we’ll make dinner without turning on a stove. In small groups, you’ll build a generous spread. Think bread, cheese, tinned fish, pickles, something sweet. You’ll learn how much to buy, how to make a board look abundant, and how to make an evening come together with ease. Then we’ll all sit down and eat what we made.
Before you leave, you’ll pick a date and send a real invitation. Yes, really. We’ll help you write it.

item.title: The Art of Paste Paper — Sun Oct 25, 10:00 AM — North Bay Letterpress Arts
item.description: Paste paper is one of the oldest decorated papers used by bookbinders, and can be found in books that are centuries old. Hundreds of years ago (a tradition that continues today), bookbinders would sometimes use up their leftover bookbinding paste by adding pigment to the mixture and brushing it out on surfaces to make decorative papers used in bookbinding. They would make strokes or stipple patterns with a brush in the paste, or use tools to draw or comb designs in the paper and then let it dry. One of the distinctive qualities of paste paper is the rich 3-dimensional patterns and designs. This is achieved because when the paste is first applied to the paper and a pattern is made, the paste is thick with peaks and valleys. As the paper dries, the paste is sucked flat into the paper, leaving a 3-dimensional pattern on a 2-dimensional surface. During this workshop students will learn about the history of paste paper.
